title: You don't have a strategy problem, you have a gap

channel.name: Andrew Builds (TradeNotes)
channel.appBlurb: a trading journal and performance analytics app

body.hook: You don't have a strategy problem. You have a gap.
body.promise: It sits between two sentences you can write in a minute. Most traders only write one.

beats.narration: Sentence one is the plan. Setup, risk, exit. That is the easy one.

scene.label: Sentence 1: before
scene.text: Pullback setup. Small risk. Stop under the low.
scene.caption: That is the easy one.

beats.narration: Sentence two is what you actually did, written before you see the result. The order is the trick.
beats.visual_query: what you actually did, before the result

scene.label: Sentence 2: after
scene.text: Entered early. Moved the stop. Held too long.
scene.caption: Write it before the result.

beats.narration: Here is why. Once you see the result, memory edits the story. A win after a broken rule feels like skill.

scene.sub: A lucky win looks like skill.

beats.narration: Write both, and the gap stops being a feeling. It becomes a count you can watch.

scene.label: trades where plan and action match
scene.caption: SAMPLE count. A number, not a feeling.

beats.narration: I built TradeNotes, my own trading journal, so I'm biased. It keeps both sentences on every trade, side by side.
So a new strategy would not close it. The gap is between your plan and your actions, and it follows you. A plan never removes the risk of loss.

body.cta: On your next trade, write sentence two before you check the result. Not financial advice.

cta.title: TradeNotes
cta.tagline: Write the plan. Write what you did. Then look at the result.

post.ytTitle: You don't have a strategy problem. You have a gap.
post.ytDesc: The gap between your plan and what you actually did is easy to miss, because most journals only record the plan or the result. This short shows the two sentences worth writing on every trade, and why the second one should be written before you look at the result. The count on screen is SAMPLE data, not real trades. Following a plan does not remove the risk of loss; a journal only gives you evidence about your own behavior. I built TradeNotes, so I'm biased. Part 2 of 5. Educational content only, not financial advice.
post.tiktok: You don't have a strategy problem. You have a gap, and it sits between two sentences most traders never both write. Sample data, education only, not financial advice. I built TradeNotes.
